intent: Return wheel_track to 0.10 m to recover the oval finish rate lost at 0.09 m, keep mass at 0.6 kg, and shorten the body to 0.10 m to lower yaw inertia and test whether the s-bend and slalom turn response improves. The sensor array is unchanged, since line loss is zero and sensing is not the limit.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) Narrowing the track below 0.10 m overshoots or destabilises the oval, so 0.10 m is the better track. (2) On the s-bend and slalom, the limit is yaw inertia rather than track width, so a shorter body at 0.6 kg should raise progress above 0.13 and bring max_error below 0.06 m. (3) If the s-bend and slalom still show max_error near 0.062 with progress unchanged, the body-length lever is weak and the next step should be to test mass alone (0.5 kg) or to revisit sensor lead (y 0.03). Please report per-track values, especially s-bend and slalom progress, max_error and steering_oscillation, and the oval finish rate.
rationale: Iteration 5 (wheel_track 0.09, mass 0.6, body 0.12 x 0.12) scored 193.5, below iteration 4's 256.4. Oval finish rate fell from 65% to 35%, which is below the 55% floor, and line loss stayed at zero. On the s-bend and slalom, progress barely moved (0.132 and 0.091, against 0.127 and 0.093) and max_error stayed at about 0.062, at the off-track floor. Narrowing the track did not fix turn response; it cost oval stability and gave almost no gain on the other tracks. The Integrator's rule for an oval finish rate below 55% with zero line loss is to return wheel_track to 0.10 m and keep mass at 0.6 kg. The s-bend progress of 0.132 is above the 0.127 overshoot trigger, so I do not read this as overshoot. The s-bend and slalom still end off_track at max_error near 0.06 m with progress below 0.3, which points to a shorter, lighter body next. Yaw inertia scales with mass times (body_length^2 + body_width^2), so a shorter body at the same mass should turn more readily. I therefore set wheel_track 0.10 m, body_length 0.10 m, mass 0.6 kg, keeping the validated sensor array (x = -0.08 to 0.08 at 0.04 m spacing, y 0.05, 0.016 m footprint), wheel_radius 0.03 m and body_width 0.12 m fixed. Expected result: oval finish rate back to about 55% or higher, and s-bend or slalom progress above 0.13 with max_error still near 0.06 m. The contract text says body_length has no direct dynamics effect, which conflicts with its yaw-inertia formula. The measured change in s-bend and slalom progress will show which one applies.
